title: Sustainability and Human Impact
seo_title: Sustainability Worksheets: Fishery Models, Population and Human Impact (Earth Science)
standard_text: Create a computational simulation to illustrate the relationships among management of natural resources, the sustainability of human populations, and biodiversity. Evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on sustainability and human impact (NGSS HS-ESS3-3, HS-ESS3-4): fishery models, population growth, resource use and technologies that reduce pollution. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Take no more than nature replaces.
key_sub: Model resource use, then test solutions with before-and-after data.
body_html:
How to think about it

Use resources no faster than nature can replace them.

  • Fishery model: next year = stock + growth − catch. A catch is sustainable if it is no more than the growth.
  • Growing populations use more resources: total = use per person × people. Rule of 70: doubling time ≈ 70 ÷ growth rate (%).
  • Technologies (scrubbers, catalytic converters, drip irrigation, wildlife crossings) reduce impacts. Judge them with data: percent reduction = (before − after) ÷ before × 100.
Example

10,000 fish, grow 20%, catch 1,500. Next year?

10,000 + 2,000 − 1,500

Answer: 10,500 fish

Example

Pollution 80 → 20 tonnes. Percent reduction?

(80 − 20) ÷ 80 × 100

Answer: 75%

Common mistakes

  • Thinking any catch is sustainable as long as fish remain.
  • Thinking population grows by the same amount every year.
  • Using before − after as the percent reduction.

faq.a: The yearly catch is no more than the number of fish the population adds each year, so the stock does not shrink over time.

faq.q: How does population growth affect resources?
faq.a: Total use is the use per person times the number of people, so a growing population uses more water, land and energy unless each person uses less.

faq.q: How do engineers judge a solution to pollution?
faq.a: They measure the problem before and after the solution, calculate the percent reduction, and weigh the benefits against costs and side effects.
